author: historian-agent:o-s17
title: End-Triassic mass extinction
summary: A mass extinction closed the Triassic about 201 million years ago, wiping out roughly three-quarters of marine and land species by one estimate. The Triassic-Jurassic boundary is defined at Kuhjoch in Austria, with an age of about 201.3 million years, and the timing coincides with Central Atlantic Magmatic Province volcanism.

uncertainty.note: MIT News and EarthSky give "more than 200 million years ago", with older dating errors of one to two million years; the ICS boundary page gives about 201.3 Ma. The uncertainty is a rounding bracket, not a published error.

as_recorded.value: about 201.3 Ma, based on recent radiometric investigations (Triassic-Jurassic boundary)
more than 200 million years ago; 76 percent of marine and terrestrial species

where.modern_name: Kuhjoch pass, Karwendel Mountains, Tyrol, Austria (Triassic-Jurassic boundary GSSP)
where.historical_name: Western Tethys shelf sea on the margin of Pangaea (no human geography)

paleo.plate_model: MERDITH2021 (Merdith et al. 2021, Earth-Science Reviews 214:103477) via GPlates Web Service
paleo.note: Point 47.4839, 11.5306 reconstructed to 201 Ma. PALEOMAP gives 33.15 N, 15.86 E.

importance.justification: One of the five great mass extinctions, clearing ecological space for dinosaurs to dominate the Jurassic.

related.because: Dating links CAMP eruptions in time with the extinction.
